In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of determining whether a class of {0, 1,..., n} valued functions can be learned in polynomial time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class of {0,..., n}-valued function is PAC-learnable if and only if its VC-dimension is finite.

the VC-dimension is a necessary and sufficient condition for learning a class of {0,1}-valued functions in the standard PAC learning model, and for learning any multi-valued function in the "robustr" variant of the PAC learning model.
the VC-dimension is the only notion of dimension that is relevant to PAC learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VC-dimension is not a unique characterization of learnability for {0,...,n}-valued functions.
, in the context of {0, 1}-valued functions, the VC-dimension is the unique notion of dimension which is a necessary and sufficient condition for learning.
we provide a unified approach to the study of learnability for classes of multi-valued function, and a number of new characterizations for the learnability of such classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a single, simple, general characterization for learning in all these settings.
there are many different ways in which the concept of VC-dimension may be generalized to the multi-valued case, and that the choice of the generalization depends on the learning task at hand.

, in the multi-valued setting, the PAC learnability is determined by a number of parameters that are not necessarily related to one another, and that each of these parameters can be used to define a notion of dimension.
